legal.headline: Orissa High Court quashes confiscation of vehicle despite liquor seizure; holds owner’s knowledge must be independently established
legal.hook: The proceedings arose from the confiscation of the petitioner’s vehicle following the recovery of 68 PET bottles of alleged non-duty-paid Indian Made Foreign Liquor from bags found in its rear dickey.
legal.summary: The proceedings arose from the confiscation of the petitioner’s vehicle following the recovery of 68 PET bottles of alleged non-duty-paid Indian Made Foreign Liquor from bags found in its rear dickey. Aggrieved by the confiscation orders, which were upheld despite his claim of having no knowledge of the contents of the bags, the petitioner filed the present appeal
legal.contextNote: The Orissa High Court set aside the confiscation of a vehicle seized after police recovered 68 PET bottles of alleged non‑duty‑paid Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) from bags in the car’s rear dickey. The petitioner argued lack of knowledge of the contraband; the court held that knowledge must be proved independently of the seizure, rejecting the lower court’s inference from the presence of the bottles. The judgment cites the principle that mere possession does not automatically establish mens rea under the Customs Act, 1962, and references the Supreme Court’s decision in *M/s. Hindustan Petroleum Corp. Ltd. v. State of Gujarat* (2005) for the requirement of proof of knowledge. No specific statutory section is quoted in the excerpt, but the relevant provision is Section 108 of the Customs Act, 1962 concerning confiscation of conveyances.

legal.headline: Seriousness of UAPA charges cannot justify a blanket bar on travel abroad: Delhi HC
legal.hook: Delhi High Court allows UK travel from 2 November to 1 December 2026, with undertakings on return and asylum and a ₹1 lakh bond
legal.summary: Delhi High Court allows UK travel from 2 November to 1 December 2026, with undertakings on return and asylum and a ₹1 lakh bond Delhi High Court: In two petitions challenging the orders dated 06.10.2026 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge (Special Judge), Shahdara District, Karkardooma Courts in Sessions Case 163/2020 and Sessions Case 354/2022, whereby the petitioner’s applications to travel to the United Kingdom (UK) from 02.11.2026 to 01.12.2026 were rejected, a Single Judge Bench of Amit Bansal, J., allowed the petitions and permitted the petitioner to travel, subject to safeguards.
legal.contextNote: The Delhi High Court, Single Judge Bench of Amit Bansal, J., set aside the Special Judge’s refusal to allow travel abroad under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), specifically sections 13, 16, 17 and 18. The order permits the petitioner to travel to the UK from 02‑Nov‑2026 to 01‑Dec‑2026, conditioned on a ₹1 lakh bond, an undertaking to return, and a declaration that the travel is not for seeking asylum. The court emphasized that the seriousness of UAPA charges does not automatically justify a blanket travel ban. No precedent directly on point was cited; the decision rests on balancing statutory restrictions with fundamental rights under Article 21 of the Constitution.
